# Selected protected EMDF carrier pipeline addendum

Scope: selected ordinary 48 kHz, 1024 kbps, one independent substream. This addendum defines the observed transport planner/writer boundary and outer publication gate. It does not generate or authenticate the protected EMDF body and does not reproduce ordinary codec audio frames.

The native planner request is signed I32 body bytes, excluding the four-byte sync/length prefix. For positive requests it selects the first block using `<=2040 -> block 2`, `2041..2551 -> block 1`, and `>=2552 -> block 0`. There are six zero-based block slots, with first capacity 507 bytes and later capacities 511 bytes. A periodic enabled prefix at counter wrap (period 62) reduces block 0 capacity by 8 bytes, making the selected tested maximum 3054 instead of 3062. Plans that leave residual bytes return 1 after mutating enabled/first-block/segment/counter fields; no rollback is observed. The caller's propagation of planner failure is not established.

For the selected four natural AU cases the body is a single fragment at substream 0, independent stream 0, block 2. The reservation emits a present bit, then a 9-bit skip length equal to body bytes plus the four-byte sync/length prefix; the saved body cursor follows those ten bits. The writer places marker bytes `58 38`, a 16-bit big-endian body length, then the body. The four bodies are 422, 316, 320 and 316 bytes, with bit cursors 10048, 11950, 11932 and 11966. Their actual source-to-queue token, descriptor, serialized-storage pointer, carrier pointer and final published-frame joins are in `NATIVE-AU-JOINS.json`.

The outer publication gate has threshold 3072 samples and hop 1536. It exposes valid bytes only when updated progress is strictly greater than threshold. Across six calls, progress is 0, 1536, 3072, 4608, 4608, 4608, 4608; valid lengths are 0, 0, 4096, 4096, 4096, 4096. The gate progress saturates at 4608 and is not a source-sample clock. Published AU ordinals are assigned only to nonzero outer valid lengths: AU 0..3 correspond to frontend/parent calls 3..6 and JOC producer calls 2..5. Earlier R21 labels that counted internal warmup outputs as published AUs are withdrawn.

`2040/2041/2551/2552` boundary calls are actual controlled planner/writer primitive cases with sufficient non-overlapping owned buffers. They do not claim that the selected natural JOC profile generates bodies that large. Full-encoder failure propagation, overlapping buffers, absolute ADM/host clock mapping, EOF/reset and body generation/authentication remain outside this package.
